title: clipfeed
subtitle: bisaya meme music video feed

scenes.heading: what is clipfeed
scenes.narration: Clipfeed is a Bisaya meme music TikTok feed plus Spotify home. The question: how does one Cloudflare Worker serve video, likes, and chat?

scenes.heading: product requirements
scenes.narration: It must scroll fyp video feed, upload clips with transcripts, live chat during playback, heart clips with counts. It keeps private admin and inbox, with fast global video start.

scenes.heading: client and edge
scenes.narration: The fyp app is the Next.js browser feed and home player. The edge guard checks admin, inbox and CSRF. The worker host renders the app on clipfeed.com.

scenes.heading: api and video
scenes.narration: The ingest api is eighty one route handlers for clips and uploads. The edge cache serves clips.clipfeed.com video for a year. The clip blobs store mp4s and covers.

scenes.heading: data and realtime
scenes.narration: The d1 database holds hosted clips and chat rows. The live chat fans out websockets after persist. The like counter tallies hearts and blocks floods.

scenes.heading: auth and helpers
scenes.narration: The google login signs users and gates admin. The inbound mail forwards email previews to inbox. The voice text transcribes uploads with Scribe.

scenes.heading: open fyp feed
scenes.narration: You open the fyp app, and the request first hits the edge guard. The guard hands it to the worker host, which renders the page. The page asks the ingest api for the catalog, and the api reads rows from the d1 database. Then your phone streams the video from the edge cache, which pulls it from the clip blobs the first time.

scenes.heading: back of envelope
scenes.narration: Let's assume fifty thousand daily users and twenty clips per visit. That is about four reads per second avg, ten times at peak evening. These are estimates, not measurements of the real app.

scenes.heading: d1 catalog overload
scenes.narration: At ten times traffic, d1 read overload hits because every feed scans all rows. The fix is snapshot cache with KV snapshots and pagination.

scenes.heading: chat fanout limit
scenes.narration: At one hundred times, single room fanout breaks one object for all sockets. The fix is shard rooms with sticky routing and gossip.

scenes.heading: cache purge pain
scenes.narration: At one hundred times deletes, purge rate limits stall year-long cache. The fix is versioned keys with hashed keys, no purge needed.

scenes.heading: design trade-offs
scenes.narration: D1 sql simple queries buys easy catalog, but full scan reads heavy costs reads. Single do simple broadcast is easy, but memory caps fanout limits rooms.

scenes.heading: clipfeed in sum
scenes.narration: Browser to edge to Worker to D1, R2, and Durable Objects. CDN streams, Scribe transcribes, sharding fixes scale.
